args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
PREPARED FOR THE PROJECT LATTICE DEAL TEAM

MEMORANDUM

TO: Project Lattice Deal Team
FROM: [Sell-Side Counsel]
RE: Disclosure Reconciliation — Schedule 3.14 (Litigation and Intellectual Property) Against Article VIII Indemnity Architecture
DATE: [Current Date]

I. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

This memorandum reconciles the litigation and intellectual property matters disclosed on Trellis BioWorks, Inc. Schedule 3.14 to the Share Purchase Agreement ("SPA") against the three indemnification architectures currently on the table for Project Lattice:

(a) the execution draft v4 of SPA Article VIII (the current sell-side draft);
(b) the second-turn markup of Article VIII transmitted by Wexler Bright LLP on behalf of Halberd Holdings LP on 30 July 2026 (the "Halberd markup"); and
(c) the Trellis Transaction Committee-approved approved indemnity positions (the "approved positions" or the "fallback").

Dollar figures cited herein appear in the referenced documents only. This analysis is quantitative where the disclosure schedule supplies amounts and qualitative where it does not.

II. THE DISCLOSED MATTERS — SUMMARY

Schedule 3.14 discloses three matters. The schedule divides them between pending matters (Items 1 and 2) and one resolved matter (Item 3).

III. ITEM-BY-ITEM RECONCILIATION

ITEM 1 — Trademark Opposition (TTAB Opposition No. 91-284772, Lumenor Devices B.V. v. Trellis BioWorks, Inc.; TRELLIGEN mark)
Status: Pending. Discovery conference held 5 May 2026.
Quantified exposure: None stated. The schedule affirmatively states that no damages are claimed in the proceeding. The exposure is characterized qualitatively: the risk is potential refusal of registration of the TRELLIGEN mark and associated rebranding of the TRELLIGEN assay line. Trellis continues to use the mark at common law.

Treatment under each architecture:

(a) v4 deductible-and-cap framework. Because no dollar amount is assigned to Item 1 in the schedule and no Losses figure is supplied, Item 1 would need to be quantified at the time of an indemnity claim. If a loss materialized (e.g., rebranding costs), it would be aggregated with other Section 8.2(a) Losses and would be subject to the $400,000 true deductible (recovery only of the excess over $400,000) and the $12,000,000 aggregate cap.

(b) Halberd markup. Under the Halberd markup, Item 1 would fall within new Section 8.2(d) (Special Indemnity), as one of "the matters disclosed on Schedule 3.14." The special indemnity is uncapped, not subject to the deductible or the cap, and survives until expiration of applicable statutes of limitation. Any rebranding or registration costs arising out of Item 1 would therefore be recoverable in full from Sellers with no deductible, no cap, no survival limit tied to the 36-month general survival period, and without exhausting the escrow.

(c) Approved positions fallback. Under the approved positions, a special indemnity is acceptable for Item 1, provided the aggregate special-indemnity cap is $2,500,000, survival is 24 months, and the special indemnity does not extend to resolved matters. Item 1 is a pending matter and would therefore be within scope. Its qualitative/quantified exposure would be measured against the $2,500,000 cap. To the extent no dollar loss is quantified now, the cap bounds Trellis's maximum exposure under the special indemnity.

ITEM 2 — Customer Dispute (Bexley Clinical Partners LLC; pre-litigation demand)
Status: Pending, pre-litigation. Written demand dated 3 April 2026; no suit filed. Trellis denied liability in its 24 April 2026 response. Insurance carrier noticed 28 April 2026; coverage position reserved.
Quantified exposure: $1,850,000 — the amount demanded by Bexley Clinical Partners LLC for alleged assay lot failures under the 2024 Supply Agreement.

Treatment under each architecture:

(a) v4 deductible-and-cap framework. If Bexley ultimately recovers on any claim, the $1,850,000 demand figure (or any lesser resolved amount) would be aggregated with other Section 8.2(a) Losses. Because the v4 structure employs a true deductible, Trellis would bear the first $400,000 of aggregate Losses, and recovery above that threshold would be payable only for the excess. At the $1,850,000 level, Trellis's exposure net of the deductible (assuming this were the only claim) would be approximately $1,450,000, well within the $12,000,000 cap.

(b) Halberd markup. Item 2 squarely falls within the proposed special indemnity (new Section 8.2(d)) as a disclosed Schedule 3.14 matter. Under the Halberd structure, the $1,850,000 demand would be recoverable from Sellers without any deductible, without any cap, without exhausting the escrow (per the Section 8.5 conforming change), and would survive until statutes of limitation expire. The special indemnity therefore converts a $1,850,000 demand into potentially uncapped seller exposure that is not subject to the negotiated cap structure.

(c) Approved positions fallback. Item 2 is a pending matter and thus eligible for the special indemnity under the approved positions if all four conditions are met: (i) scope limited to Items 1 and 2; (ii) aggregate cap of $2,500,000; (iii) survival of 24 months; and (iv) resolved matters excluded. At the currently-claimed $1,850,000, Item 2 would consume $1,850,000 of the $2,500,000 aggregate special-indemnity cap, leaving only $650,000 for Item 1 under the combined cap.

ITEM 3 — OSHA Citation (Citation No. 1829445, Region IV)
Status: Resolved. Penalty of $46,500 paid in full on 17 March 2026; abatement certified 2 March 2026. The schedule states this matter "is closed" and is "disclosed as a resolved matter only."
Quantified exposure: $46,500 — the penalty, which has been paid.

Treatment under each architecture:

(a) v4 deductible-and-cap framework. Because the $46,500 penalty has been fully paid and the matter resolved, no residual Losses are expected. Should any residual claim arise, the $46,500 would fall below the $400,000 deductible and would not be recoverable absent aggregation with other losses.

(b) Halberd markup. The Halberd special indemnity as drafted covers "any and all Losses arising out of or relating to the matters disclosed on Schedule 3.14" — which as written includes Item 3 as a resolved matter. An uncapped, non-deductible, statute-of-limitation-surviving special indemnity would sweep in already-resolved matters for which the $46,500 has been paid, creating residual exposure beyond the resolved settlement.

(c) Approved positions fallback. The approved positions expressly require that resolved matters — including Schedule 3.14 Item 3 — be excluded from any special indemnity (IP-4(iv)). The deal team's approved instruction is that a special indemnity may include only Items 1 and 2 (the pending matters). Item 3's inclusion would be out of policy.

IV. AGGREGATE QUANTIFIED EXPOSURE OF PENDING DISCLOSED MATTERS

The pending matters (Items 1 and 2) on Schedule 3.14 carry one quantified dollar amount: Item 2's $1,850,000 demand from Bexley Clinical Partners. Item 1 has no assigned dollar amount (the schedule affirmatively states no damages are claimed). Therefore:

Aggregate quantified exposure of pending disclosed matters: $1,850,000.

This figure represents the claimed, not established, amount, and does not include any quantification for Item 1 (which is qualitative — the cost of potential rebranding of the TRELLIGEN line). If Item 1 rebranding costs were later valued, that amount would need to be added to the $1,850,000 for a full aggregate picture.

V. FLAGGED EXCLUSION — ITEM 3 (OSHA CITATION)

The approved positions require that Schedule 3.14 Item 3 (the resolved OSHA citation, Citation No. 1829445) be expressly excluded from any special indemnity (IP-4(iv)). The reason: Item 3 is a resolved and closed matter — the $46,500 penalty has been paid in full and abatement certified. The deal team's policy is that a special indemnity is authorized only for pending matters (Items 1 and 2), because including resolved matters would expose sell-side to uncapped residual claims on matters that have already been closed, settled, and paid. Under the Halberd markup's broad "matters disclosed on Schedule 3.14" language, Item 3 would be swept into the special indemnity as drafted, which is why the approved-positions fallback — and any Trellis counter-draft — must carve it out.

VI. ARCHITECTURE COMPARISON — CAP AND DEDUCTIBLE DELTAS

For reference against the $120,000,000 Purchase Price:

| Element | v4 | Halberd Markup | Approved Fallback |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deductible/basket | $400,000 true deductible | $250,000 tipping basket | True deductible, floor $300,000 |
| Cap (general) | $12,000,000 (10%) | $30,000,000 (25%) | $18,000,000 (15%) |
| Survival (general) | 18 months | 36 months | 24 months max |
| Special indemnity | None | Uncapped, all of Schedule 3.14 | $2,500,000 cap, Items 1 & 2 only, 24 months |
| Order of recovery | Escrow first | Special claims bypass escrow | [per v4] |

The Halberd markup's $30,000,000 cap and $250,000 tipping basket each exceed the approved fallback authority by a material margin; any indication that those numbers are acceptable would require Special Committee approval per the approved positions memo. The approved fallback cap of $18,000,000 (15%) is the maximum within delegated authority.

VII. CONCLUSION

The disclosure schedule's quantified pending exposure is $1,850,000 (Item 2). Item 1's exposure is qualitative and unquantified. The v4 structure would absorb the quantified exposure within the $12,000,000 cap and subject to the $400,000 deductible; the Halberd markup's special indemnity would remove all constraints (no deductible, no cap, statute-of-limitation survival, escrow bypass); and the approved fallback would admit pending matters (Items 1 and 2) into a $2,500,000 capped, 24-month special indemnity that expressly excludes resolved Item 3. The deal team should treat Item 3's exclusion from any special indemnity as non-negotiable under current delegated authority, and any move toward the Halberd cap or basket figures requires Special Committee escalation.

— END OF MEMORANDUM —
